rows.note: Use this for the familiar bean sprout, especially in food contexts.

example.english: I found a bean sprout in my noodles.
example.traditional: 我喺碗麵入面搵到一條豆芽。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai2 wun2 min6 jap6 min6 wan2 dou3 jat1 tiu4 dau6 ngaa4

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice when a seed or plant germinates on its own.

example.english: These beans finally sprout after soaking for a few days.

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a small new plant growth or a just-germinated young plant.

example.english: The seeds I planted have finally started to sprout.
example.traditional: 我種落嘅種子終於發芽喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung3 lok6 ge3 zung2 zi2 zung1 jyu1 faat3 ngaa4 laa3

rows.note: Use this when something suddenly appears or emerges from a surface, including whiskers or new businesses.

example.english: Several new restaurants sprout up nearby even though the shop has only been open for a few months.

rows.note: Use this for edible sprouts as a food category when you do not mean specifically bean sprouts.

example.english: This kind of sprout is a common salad ingredient.
example.traditional: 呢種芽菜係沙律常用嘅食材。
example.jyutping: nei1 zung2 ngaa4 coi3 hai6 saa1 leot2 soeng4 jung6 ge3 sik6 coi4

rows.note: Use this result construction when you deliberately grow seeds until they germinate, rather than simply reporting that they 發芽.

example.english: I finally got the beans to sprout.
example.traditional: 我終於種到啲豆發芽喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 jyu1 zung3 dou3 di1 dau6 faat3 ngaa4 laa3
